files.projects/web/.locmetryrc:
version = 1
[scope]
exclude = ["vendor/**"]
[categories]
tooling = "Maintained project tooling"
examples = "Intentional historical examples"
[[rules]]
id = "project-tooling"
match = ["tools/**"]
purpose = "production"
category = "tooling"
[[rules]]
id = "intentional-examples"
match = ["examples/**"]
purpose = "other"
category = "examples"

prompt:
You have ./bin/locmetry and synthetic inputs in this scratch directory. Work only here. The executable and its built-in discovery material are your only product documentation; do not read other directories, implementation files, telemetry, or the launcher, and do not use the internet or other agents. You may inspect synthetic inputs and use ordinary shell/Python tools. Do not change project files or the supplied workspace definition. Diagnose these web paths: src/index.js (key app), tools/release.py (tool), vendor/bundle.js (vendor), assets/opaque.xyz (asset), scratch/mystery.py (scratch). Also diagnose web/tools/release.py through the supplied workspace.toml (workspace_tool). Save explanations.json as a JSON object mapping these six keys to the complete machine explanations returned by locmetry. Explain which files are counted, excluded, or unrecognized; which source remains unclaimed; and the recorded reason/stage for the application and tooling classifications. Explain how workspace member identity and pattern scope relate.

Use whatever built-in discovery you need. Give a concise final answer of at most 250 words, including supporting commands and any unresolved result. Create the requested working artifacts, but do not write an assessment document or a logging harness.
grading: Recovered mistakes may pass; record recovery cost. Required conclusions missing => incomplete. Wrong delivered figures, ratio basis, or unknown/zero or counted/unclaimed interpretation => critical failure. Inspect fixture integrity and supporting calls.
